advisory.title: Non-constant-time mask generation and `u128` comparisons
advisory.description:
## Summary

The `ctutils::Choice` type has mask generation functions for each unsigned
integer size (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `u128`). These are `const fn` and
therefore can't reuse the `asm!`-backed mask generation in the `cmov` crate
that's otherwise used to ensure constant-time.

In releases prior to v0.4.4, the generated code from these functions could
include a branch on commonly used platforms. This has been corrected in this
release and now verified on several platforms using BINSEC.

Additionally, `u128` comparison operations provided via `ctutils::Choice` and
intended to work in constant-time were generating branches on 32-bit targets.
This has been resolved via a special case implementation of these functions
for such targets.

## Impact

Branch instructions on secret values can potentially leak such values via
covert channels. This can enable attackers to potentially recover such secrets.

## Resolution

This has been resolved by calling `Choice::to_u8()` when generating the mask,
which in turn uses `black_box` as an optimization barrier. Verification that
this resulted in the desired change in the generated assembly across a variety
of target CPU architectures was performed by BINSEC, which now runs
automatically in CI using `cargo checkct`.

advisory.title: unsafe-libyaml is unmaintained
advisory.description:
The [repository](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) was archived by
its owner on 2024-03-25 and is read-only. The last release is 0.2.11
(March 2024).

`unsafe-libyaml` is a machine translation of libyaml's C code into unsafe
Rust (c2rust). Bugs found in it will not be fixed upstream. It is used by
`serde_yaml` (itself deprecated) and by forks such as `serde_yaml_ng`.

## Alternatives

Consider a YAML parser written in safe Rust, for example:

- [saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/saphyr) ([serde-saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/serde-saphyr) for serde users)
- [noyalib](https://crates.io/crates/noyalib)

advisory.title: Potential use-after-free due to lack of panic safety in `LruCache::pop()`
advisory.description:
`LruCache::pop()` in `lru` was not panic-safe. If the `Drop` implementation of a stored key panics during `pop()`, `self.detach()` is never called, leaving dangling pointers in the internal doubly-linked list.

A subsequent cache operation that triggers eviction can then dereference these dangling pointers:
- The node is freed from the map, but remains linked in the LRU list due to the skipped `detach()` call
- When a new insertion causes eviction, the LRU traversal encounters the dangling pointer
- This results in a write to already-freed memory during the eviction process

## Impact

- **CWE-416 (Use-After-Free):** memory corruption when subsequent cache operations access freed node pointers in the linked list
- **CWE-415 (Double Free):** potential heap corruption when the same memory is freed multiple times

Both types of undefined behavior can be invoked in safe Rust, but only if unwinding panics are enabled and `std::panic::catch_unwind` is used with key types that have potentially-panicking `Drop` implementations.

## Fix

Fixed in `lru` 0.18.2 by detaching the node from the linked list before freeing it and dropping the key ([lru-rs#238](https://github.com/jeromefroe/lru-rs/pull/238)).

advisory.title: `IterMut` violates Stacked Borrows by invalidating internal pointer
advisory.description:
Affected versions of this crate contain a soundness issue in the `IterMut`
iterator implementation. The `IterMut::next` and `IterMut::next_back`
methods temporarily create an exclusive reference to the key when
dereferencing the internal node pointer.

This invalidates the shared pointer held by the internal `HashMap`,
violating Stacked Borrows rules.
